title: Nash equilibrium
src: John Nash, Equilibrium Points in N-Person Games, 1950
idea: A Nash equilibrium is a situation where nobody can do better by changing only their own choice, even if everyone would prefer something else.
apply: When a bad situation is stable, look at what each person would lose by moving alone, then coordinate a move together.
who: A concert crowd, where everyone ends up standing.

items.x: Now the row behind cannot see

scenes.nar: At a concert, everyone is seated and can see fine. One person stands up, and now the people behind them cannot see.
Soon everyone stands. The view is the same as at the start, only with tired feet, and anyone who sits alone sees nothing.
That is a Nash equilibrium. Nobody can do better by changing alone, so the crowd stays stuck. The way out is to change together.

items.x: Organizers ask the front rows to sit

scenes.nar: At a better venue, the organizers ask the front rows to stay seated. Everyone agrees, and everyone sees without standing.
